_readme: Tree's taste thresholds, read by scripts/social/check-drafts.mjs (and lib/photo-reuse.mjs, lib/lessons.mjs callers) via scripts/social/lib/strategy-params.mjs. Tree owns this file: edit it by PR, put the evidence for the change in that section's `why`, report it in the weekly plan; Marjorie's weekly Fable review keeps, reverts or adjusts it. Lands without a founder merge. NOT here, and not switchable from here: the founder-owned guardrails in docs/social/guardrails.md (credit, rights, platform limits, the approval stamp). A missing or invalid field falls back to the built-in default, which equals the pre-2026-10-01 behaviour. `mediaKind: "card"` also needs lib/queue-schema.mjs to list it (posting-path PR) before a card draft clears validate-queue.

media.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline, equal to the prior hard-coded gate plus `card` (owner: Tree decides cards/pictures/other; a card is a committed PNG rendered from /api/share-card, credited "Long Live", never lyrics).

siteScreen.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: the 2026-08-31 audit found site-screen on 7 of the last 10 posted IG items (social/posted/); kept as a launch-only carousel behind a Taylor photo until Tree has evidence to widen it.

photoReuse.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: lesson L001 (6 firings, social/lessons.md) - a photo may repeat only across the IG and X halves of one campaign; the IG-history window is the last 10 posted IG items.

photoMix.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: advisory only (a warning, never a failure) when fewer than 70% of the last 10 posted IG items were mediaKind photo and this draft is not one either; the 2026-08-12 Taylor-photo standard made photos the default.

pairing.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: owner 2026-08-25/2026-09-10 'one idea goes out to X, Instagram... all together'; a per-item singlePlatformReason is still the one exemption.

openers.why: 2026-11-09 (#6747, ops-fixer): the first-word diversity cap Tree's note below asked for has LANDED — `firstWordWindow`/`firstWordMaxRepeats` fail an Instagram draft whose first word already opened more than 2 of the last 7 posted Instagram items (so the 3rd repeat fails), naming the word and the count. It is the standing answer to the stem-by-stem whack-a-mole the `bannedOpeners` list had turned into: `did you know` (2026-08-11) → `okay`/`ok` (2026-11-02) → `i cannot stop`/`i will never`/`i did not expect` (2026-11-09) were all the same formula one word over, and all of them cleared the 6-word reuse gate because words 2-6 differ. Instagram only, and nothing here bans the first person — `i went digging through The Decode` is still strategy §2's voice working, it just cannot be the opening word of a third post in seven. ||| 2026-11-09 (Tree, week-of-11-09 plan): THREE reaction-stems added — `i cannot stop`, `i will never`, `i did not expect`. The 2026-11-02 `okay`/`ok` gate below worked exactly as intended (zero posts have opened on either since 10-31), and the formula simply moved one word over: the six Instagram captions posted 2026-11-02 → 11-08 opened `i went digging through The Decode…` / `it's finally cardigan weather where i am…` / `this is the chapter i always forget…` / `i will never be normal about this…` / `i did not expect to tear up…` / `i cannot stop thinking about this one…` — four of six on the literal word `i`, and six of six leading on the writer's reaction before the subject arrives. All six cleared the 6-word reuse gate because words 2-6 differ every time, which is the 2026-08-11 `did you know` finding recurring for the third time under a third word. The three stems listed are the exact bodies that shipped, prefix-anchored, nothing wider. A blanket first-person ban is DELIBERATELY NOT written here: strategy §2's Voice section wants a fan in love with Taylor, and `i went digging through The Decode` is that voice working with the subject in the first clause, so banning it would narrow an approved strategy element rather than fix a formula. The real gate is a first-word diversity cap (fail an IG draft whose first word already opened ≥3 of the last 7 posted IG items), which lives in check-drafts.mjs, outside this desk's mutation rights, and is asked of Marjorie in the week-of-11-09 brief. Until it lands, §1(e) Rule 2's standing direction — the first clause carries the subject, not the writer's reaction to it — is carried on every beat in social/calendar.md. ||| 2026-11-02 (Tree, week-of-11-02 plan): two changes, both evidence-led. (1) SYNC — strategy §1(e) Rule 2 has published a 14-opener banned list since 2026-08-11 and said it was "hard-blocked by check-drafts.mjs", but this file only ever carried `did you know`, so 13 of the 14 were never actually blocked. The list is now what the doc says it is. (`a thread 🧵` is carried as `a thread` because the matcher anchors `^<phrase>\b` and a `\b` after an emoji never matches.) (2) NEW — `okay` and `ok` as first words: 4 of the 22 items posted 2026-10-20 → 2026-11-01 opened on one (10-21 IG "okay i tapped…", 10-26 IG "okay END GAME fans…", 10-30 X "ok swifties…", 10-31 IG "okay folklore track 3…"), and all 22 still cleared the 6-word reuse gate, which cannot see a shared first word when words 2-6 differ. The week-of-10-26 calendar put that shape off the menu in prose and it shipped twice anyway; a formula openers gate that misses the formula actually forming is the 2026-08-11 "did you know" finding recurring under a new word. Prefix-anchored, so only a body literally opening on the word fails. The first-6-words match still runs against the last 14 days of posts and the queue.

crossPost.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: the 2026-08-10 TTPD pair scored ~0.89 word overlap and plausibly drew X's duplicate-content 403; below 0.8 the X copy reads as its own.

xLength.why: 2026-10-01 S2 baseline: a self-imposed headroom warning under X's 280 weighted limit (the 280 limit itself is a guardrail and not tunable).

lessons.why: 2026-10-01 S2: promoting a rejection lesson into a hard gate after 3 firings is now Tree's explicit choice per lesson (set true to restore the old automatic `codify:` issue), not an automatic ratchet.
